source.title: SAMPLE COSTS TO ESTABLISH AND PRODUCE
source.publisher: UC Davis Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics / UC Cooperative Extension

priceYear.quote: Sample costs given for labor, materials, equipment and contract services are based on January 2018 figures.

acresFarmed.quote: The hypothetical farm consists of 105 contiguous acres farmed by the owner.

acresCrop.quote: Walnuts are established on 100 acres; roads, irrigation systems and farmstead occupy five acres.

interestRatePct.quote: An interest rate of 5.50 percent is used to calculate capital recovery.

operatingInterestRatePct.quote: Interest on operating capital is based on cash operating costs and is calculated monthly until harvest at a nominal rate of 5.0 percent per year.

laborMachineRate.quote: Hourly wages for workers are $14.50 for machine operators and $12.50 per hour non-machine labor.

laborNonMachineRate.quote: Hourly wages for workers are $14.50 for machine operators and $12.50 per hour non-machine labor.

fuelPriceDiesel.quote: Prices for on-farm delivery of diesel and gasoline are $2.92 and $3.46 per gallon, respectively.

fuelPriceGas.quote: Prices for on-farm delivery of diesel and gasoline are $2.92 and $3.46 per gallon, respectively.

yieldStatement.quote: The average yield over the remaining life of the orchard is assumed to be 6,000 pounds per acre.

priceStatement.quote: For this study, a projected price of $1.00 per pound is used in the tables.

costsPerAcre.title: COSTS PER ACRE TO PRODUCE WALNUTS

capitalRecoveryFormula.quote: The formula for the calculation of the annual capital recovery costs is ((Purchase Price – Salvage Value) x Capital Recovery Factor) + (Salvage Value x Interest Rate).

salvageMethod.quote: Salvage value is an estimate of the remaining value of an investment at the end of its useful life.

propertyTaxRatePct.quote: For this study, county taxes are calculated as 1 percent of the average value of the property.

machineLaborFactor.quote: Labor for operations involving machinery are 20 percent higher than the actual operation time given to account for the extra labor involved in equipment set up, moving, maintenance, work breaks, and field repair.

monthly.quote: MONTHLY COSTS PER ACRE TO PRODUCE WALNUTS

plantingLife.quote: The economic life of the orchard is assumed to be 30 years.

removalCost.note: Removal of the previous planting, charged as a pre-plant cost in the first establishment year. The studies do not charge an end-of-life removal and set the establishment asset salvage value to zero.

method.quote: Establishment cost is amortized beginning in the fifth year over the remaining 30 years of production.
